question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; Task production execution; first-principles hard-cut; permanent matched runtime/type benchmark; package and browser proof
trigger: The user authorized direct execution of the accepted shared-plugin-identity feasibility plan across Plite, Plate, feature callers, docs, doctrine, release artifacts and proof.
requirements: Use one nominal plugin descriptor family across raw Plite and Plate-authored plugins while retaining Plate product compilation.
Separate immutable authored descriptors from installed normalized records and preserve direct dependencies, conflicts, source ancestry, candidate rollback, retained portals and exact views.
Delete synthetic Plate raw descriptors, the global alias graph, name remapping and raw-versus-Plate portal dispatch without compatibility aliases.
Expose definePlugin, plugins and editor.plugin vocabulary, with public inference and no compiler carrier leaks.
Migrate architecture, math, emoji, AI and remaining feature callers in independently reviewable cohorts without feature behavior redesign.

Pass the frozen 1/32/128/512 runtime and 128-descriptor TypeScript budgets, package tests/typechecks/builds, packed release consumers, exact mounted-view browser proof, docs, doctrine, barrels and changesets.
evidenceReuse: Reused the prototype verdict and frozen acceptance laws, then rechecked them against production source. Production implementation added the permanent source-built benchmark, focused identity/publication regressions, broad Plite and Plate package suites, generated API/registry output, packed release consumers and one exact Chromium mounted-view replay. Failed type and runtime candidates were repaired at their measured owners before the final rerun.
summary: Pursue is implemented and production-proven. Plite and Plate share one nominal immutable plugin descriptor identity; Plite installation owns separate normalized records, and Plate retains only its product compiler plus a private plitejs/internal lowering bridge. Public authoring and lookup use definePlugin, plugins and editor.plugin. Synthetic descriptors, alias/name topology translation and portal dispatch adapters are deleted. The final source-built benchmark beats or matches every frozen runtime/type budget, and package, declaration, SSR, DCE, browser, docs and migration proof passes.
alternatives: Keep the extension/plugin split and adapter: rejected because production source now proves the translation can be deleted while preserving both layer jobs.
Move Plate product compilation into Plite: rejected because configuration, stores, schema and rendering remain Plate-owned product policy.
Keep name-based replacement for independently authored same-name descriptors: rejected; direct descriptor identity is the dependency and conflict law.
Publish RuntimePlugin aliases or a public compiled descriptor family: rejected because either recreates dual identity or leaks the compiler boundary.
Chosen target: one frozen nominal descriptor family, separate installed records, direct descriptor topology and a private Plate-to-Plite compiled-entry bridge.
proofLimits: Production proof covers 40 warm samples after eight warmups for each 1/32/128/512 cohort, three TypeScript runs over 64 raw plus 64 Plate descriptors, all Plite and Plate package partitions, packed NodeNext/Bundler/Node/SSR/DCE consumers and one Chromium exact mounted-view test. It does not claim a cross-browser matrix, published registry release or external application migration. A broader CLI aggregate encountered an existing watcher timeout cascade after 57 passing tests; the seven migration-focused CLI tests and package/release boundaries pass.
